title: Need advice
author: northern_mastadon
selftext:
Hi everyone, 

I will start by saying, I have always wanted to created a game and never had the time to learn until in May I decided to get into it. Using AI and following its guidance has taught me a lot. (Usage of blender/meshy/accurig/docker/etc) I'm nowhere near as experienced on it as everyone here but I can more or less figure stuff out myself with time and YouTube videos.

I'm trying to create a semi modern/fantasy city with quests and etc. I have a hard time getting AI (chatgpt 156$ pro) to generate the buildings/NPC etc it all comes up like a PS1 game graphic. When I compare to how everyone is able to get something close to ps3-ps4 graphic type of games out of it. Also when it creates people that it designed in 2d to 3d it's not able rig them properly.

It also keeps reworking on the same things non stop, I try to switch from sol to terra to Astra etc as I was told not to do everything in Astra but complicated stuff like 3d.

I don't know how to give proper prompts, I mostly chat with AI to get things done as I am learning in the process following what it does. 

When we made the blueprint, everything was separated in phases so every time we were done with one I would ask to get to next phase etc but it would still turn around and do other stuffs.

Here are my questions: 

\- Are there any advices anyone can give me on how to make proper prompts and better use of the different AI tool?

\- What can I use to make a few 3d cities filled with interactive npc? What would be a prompts for it? 

Sorry for the long post, appreciate all the advices and help

Thank you.

comments.author: because-potato
comments.body: Learn how to use unreal, then have codex write your scripts. Stop trying to single prompt entire games. You’ll get slop out. If you’re not willing to put in the work, you’ll never get a good game out of AI.

replies.author: northern_mastadon
replies.body:
Thank you, im trying atm getting 2d out of ai, then 3d out of meshy, having a bit of hard time figuring out the # of triangles to make rigs/animation work properly or often doesn't connect when I make the skeletons. 

Was just wondering how folks where able to post these single prompt stuff as when I did it, it brought weird results.

replies.author: because-potato
replies.body: They occasionally get lucky results, but the ones that look good are all a thousand miles wide, and an inch deep.

comments.author: 12OffIntx
comments.body:
Ask Astra or Fable. Here is an example prompt, just off the top of my head. I threw in Shadowrun as an example given your description but use whatever reference you want.

  
"Propose to me how you would handle creating a 3D city with a blend of fantasy and modern aesthetic with a target fidelity of ShadowRun Hong Kong. 3D characters of matching fidelity need to be ale to navigate and interact with thins in the city. Tools available are Blender via MCP, Meshy, accurig, and a chatGPT Pro account and free or open source resources without commercial limitations. Human time is ample and project is not under particular time constraints. Engine choice is up to you - Godot, Unity and Unreal are options as well as something more custom if preferred."

  
If that actually sounded relevant to you, DM me and I'll give you what Astra spit out in response to that prompt (thanks to the forced refresh 36 hours before my natural refresh OpenAI).

comments.author: ribalantoun
comments.body:
the rig not connecting usually isn't about triangle count. auto-riggers like AccuRig care about pose and shape: arms away from the body, legs apart, hands empty, one closed mesh. image-to-3D from a character drawn in a dynamic pose gives you arms fused to the hips and a sword grown into the hand, and then no skeleton sits right whatever the poly count. so when chatgpt makes the 2D design, ask it for a front-facing A-pose version as a separate step, and send that to meshy instead of the nice pose.



on the PS1 look, a lot of what reads as PS3/PS4 in the posts here is lighting and materials rather than the models. before regenerating a building for the fifth time, drop one into a scene with a proper sky light, some fog and shadows turned on, and see how far that moves it.



and because-potato's point stands even if it came out blunt. get one NPC from image to rigged to walking around in the engine, then do the next one. a city is mostly the same thing done once properly and then repeated.



I work on [Ludo.ai](http://Ludo.ai), so weigh this accordingly, but for the NPC side it does the image-to-rig part in one place: it makes a 3D model from an image or a text description and auto-rigs it, and humanoid animation presets go straight on that rig. the output is .glb files, the rigged model plus one per animation, instead of a meshy to accurig handoff. the A-pose advice still applies to whatever image you feed it.

replies.author: northern_mastadon
replies.body: Wow amazing info, thank you very much. Was  looking into buying assets but could never find the right art sets for my game. This way I can keep working on it 🔥🔥really appreciate it thx again 😁😁

comments.author: Legitimate_Major3799
comments.body: If you’re already doing 2D → Meshy → rig/animation, I wouldn’t focus too much on triangle count. Rigging usually breaks because of proportions, disconnected geometry, messy topology, or the mesh just not being prepared for deformation. I’d clean the character in Blender first and then send it through AccuRig rather than expecting the raw Meshy output to rig perfectly.

replies.author: Dracochibre
replies.body: I’d also split the workflow up more. Use Meshy for individual base characters/props, Blender + AccuRig for cleanup and rig prep, then Unreal for actually building the city. Astra/ChatGPT are probably more useful for planning, scripts, Blueprints and helping assemble everything than asking one model to generate the whole city/game in one go.

replies.author: northern_mastadon
replies.body: Thank you, will test these differently than I first did. Had a bit of rough time using ludo like I was suggested in one of the comments, 3/4 of my 3d work would be coming out without eyes. Will try your way too.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
for graphical assets, it is easier to just prompt for each character/prop/weapon/etc individually for the best results. Astra/Fable can also make 3d models now but it is not quite there yet (especially for complex characters)

look into "3d gen AI" and take your picks. 

think of "graphics preparation" as a phase. 

e.g. hopefully you have a spreadsheet of your character/props/weapons/object/environment needed for the game. Let's say your demo is only covering Act 1. Have a complete list of all the stuff involved for Act 1. Prompt each of them until you have the set. 

once you have it, then you can go back to telling Ai to work on the code
